text: Ignore — bookkeeping marker, not a finding.

`process.exit(main())` short-circuits any pending stdout flush on Windows in rare cases; the codebase's other scripts use the same pattern, so kept for consistency. If flush truncation is ever observed, switch to `process.exitCode = main()`.

The registry-length assertion (`toHaveLength(12)`) must be hand-bumped every time a health check is added — a brittle coupling. Consider replacing it with a duplicate-id assertion plus the existing per-id presence check, which catches the same real defects without going stale.

The hook is a growing flat script mixing blocking guards and advisory warnings with no section markers. Consider splitting the blocking guards into a single `node scripts/precommit-guards.js` so the checks become unit-testable and cross-platform (the shell-only guards are skipped on native Windows Git).

`cmdUnlink` runs `npm install` in the consumer directory unconditionally, even when the marker shows nothing was linked there. A guard (`if (\!linked[pkg.name]) continue`) would avoid a needless multi-second install when the user runs `dev-unlink` while already in PROD mode.

The bootstrap script has no sibling-linking logic, yet docs/references/development.md claimed it 'handles sibling linking automatically'. Documentation drift now corrected; consider adding a preflight warning when .dev-links.json exists so long-running commands surface DEV mode too.

`storeList` AC-4 timed out at the 5000ms default under full-suite parallel load but passes in isolation and on re-run — a flaky contention failure, not a regression. It spawns/loads mcp-server dist via ledger-dirs.js; give this test an explicit longer timeout (like the 15_000 used in health-checks.test.js) to stop it intermittently failing `npm test`.

Help-variant labels wider than the CMD_WIDTH column in @mistralys/cli-menu's help.ts collide with their description text (observed with 'dev-link --package persona-builder'). A width assertion or truncation in the cli-menu help renderer would catch this at render time instead of leaving each caller to guess the limit.

Original cmdUnlink ran `npm install` in every consumer directory regardless of what was linked. Caught in end-to-end validation: it rewrote the tracked `personas/package-lock.json` version field (3.32.0 -> 3.31.0, npm syncing the lock to the stale package.json version), directly violating the plan's 'never modify package-lock.json' constraint. Fixed by filtering consumers to those with an actual linked package (marker entry or live symlink). Note the underlying drift: personas/package.json says 3.31.0 while its lock file says 3.32.0 — a pre-existing version-sync gap that check-version-sync.js does not cover for lock files.
